Recent related events (events are separated by numbered tags): <1> A report from the Center for Data Innovation, published on October 10, 2023, highlighted that authorizations for some programs under the National Quantum Initiative Act (NQIA) had expired on September 30, 2023. [3] The report emphasized the critical need for the act's reauthorization to maintain U.S. leadership in the quantum field, recommending an appropriation of at least $525 million per year for fiscal years 2024 through 2028. [3] The original NQIA was signed into law in December 2018 to accelerate quantum R&D in the United States with over $1.2 billion in authorized funding over five years. [3] Following the expiration, bipartisan bills to reauthorize the National Quantum Initiative were introduced in both the House and Senate. [4, 5, 6] <2> Scientists from Quantinuum, in collaboration with researchers from QuTech at Delft University of Technology and the University of Stuttgart, have made a significant advancement in fault-tolerant quantum operations. Using the H1 quantum computer, they successfully executed a fully fault-tolerant algorithm using three logically-encoded qubits. This achievement is a crucial step toward the development of practical and reliable quantum computers capable of solving real-world problems. The experiment involved performing a one-bit addition using the smallest-known fault-tolerant circuit, which resulted in an error rate nearly an order of magnitude lower than an unencoded circuit. This breakthrough was detailed in a paper titled "Fault-Tolerant One-Bit Addition with the Smallest Interesting Colour Code" posted on arXiv. <3> IonQ is a trapped-ion quantum computing company; IonQ announced two new quantum computer models; The new models are Forte Enterprise and Tempo <4> Quantinuum announced that its researchers, in collaboration with the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) and the University of Maryland, have utilized the high precision of the H2-1 trapped-ion quantum computer to advance the understanding of exotic physics. [1] This work represents a significant step in leveraging quantum computers for scientific discovery in complex physical systems that are difficult for classical computers to simulate. [1] The team's research focused on the 'Fermi-Hubbard' model, which is crucial for investigating enigmatic phenomena like high-temperature superconductivity. [1] By successfully measuring the 'Loschmidt amplitude' within this model, the experiment demonstrated a key component of a proposed quantum computing algorithm, underscoring the H2-1's exceptional precision and high-fidelity all-to-all connectivity. <5> The U.S. National Science Foundation (NSF) announced an investment of $38 million to fund 22 grants through its Expanding Capacity in Quantum Information Science and Engineering (ExpandQISE) program. This initiative aims to broaden participation in quantum information science and engineering (QISE) by supporting innovative research and fostering collaborations between emerging research institutions and established centers. The program encourages applications from minority-serving institutions and those in jurisdictions part of the NSF Established Program to Stimulate Competitive Research (EPSCoR). Of the 22 recipient institutions, six are historically Black colleges and universities and three are Hispanic-serving institutions. The grants are divided into two tracks: Track 1 awards provide up to $800,000 over three years for individual researchers, and Track 2 awards offer up to $5 million over five years for larger teams. <6> Google announced it would enhance security in its Chrome browser by adding support for a quantum-resistant encryption algorithm. [5] Starting with the release of Chrome 116, the browser implemented X25519Kyber768 to establish symmetric secrets in TLS. [5, 9] This hybrid algorithm combines the existing X25519 elliptic curve algorithm with the quantum-resistant Kyber-768 to create a strong session key for encrypting TLS connections. [5] The initiative is designed to protect user data from the future threat of "harvest now, decrypt later" attacks, where encrypted data is collected today with the intent of decrypting it in the future using powerful quantum computers. [5] Kyber-768 was selected by the U.S. National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) as a candidate for general encryption against future quantum computing threats. [5] <7> In a collaboration between SEEQC and HQS Quantum Simulations, an HQS algorithm was successfully executed on SEEQC's System Red, a full-stack quantum computing platform. This marked the first instance of an HQS algorithm running on actual hardware and served as a significant third-party validation of the commercial readiness and performance of SEEQC's platform. The successful execution demonstrated that the SEEQC Red system possesses a stable and well-characterized noise model, which is ideal for running near-term quantum algorithms and utilizing noise mitigation techniques. HQS develops quantum algorithms aimed at accelerating commercial roadmaps in the chemistry and pharmaceutical sectors. <8> Inflection AI, a company specializing in personal artificial intelligence, announced it had raised $1.3 billion in a funding round, bringing its total funding to $1.525 billion. [1, 6, 7] The round was led by Microsoft, Reid Hoffman, Bill Gates, Eric Schmidt, and new investor NVIDIA. [1] The company stated the funds would be used to build the world's largest AI cluster, comprising 22,000 NVIDIA H100 Tensor Core GPUs, in partnership with CoreWeave and NVIDIA. [1, 3, 6] This investment is intended to support the continued development of Inflection AI's personal AI assistant, Pi, which launched in May 2023. [1, 3, 6] <9> Microsoft introduced "Copilot in Azure Quantum," an AI-powered assistant designed to aid researchers in the field of quantum computing. [2, 5] Unveiled at a virtual event, this tool is based on GPT-4 and helps users understand complex quantum concepts, write code for quantum computers, and reason through challenges in chemistry and material science using natural language. [2] The Copilot is integrated into a browser-based experience within Azure Quantum Elements and is designed to accelerate scientific discovery by combining AI with high-performance computing. [2, 3, 4] <10> On June 21, 2023, Microsoft announced Azure Quantum Elements, a new service designed to accelerate scientific discovery in chemistry and materials science. The platform integrates high-performance computing (HPC), AI, and quantum computing to significantly speed up research, with Microsoft claiming it can accelerate certain chemistry simulations by 500,000 times. A private preview of Azure Quantum Elements was scheduled to become available on June 30, 2023.

This will be achieved by integrating Classiq's end-to-end quantum software platform, which automates the development of quantum software, with OQC's pioneering quantum computing hardware. The partnership will offer users a seamless workflow that includes modeling, debugging, automatic quantum circuit synthesis, and circuit optimization, with execution on OQC's cutting-edge hardware, including the next-generation OQC Toshiko machine. The second processor, 'Heron', is a 133-qubit machine that represents IBM's most performant quantum processor to date. It achieves a three to five-fold improvement in error reduction compared to the previous 'Eagle' processor, a critical step in overcoming a major obstacle in quantum computing. Companies such as Amazon and D-Wave were highlighted as notable investment opportunities. D-Wave Quantum Inc. experienced a significant stock surge, fueled by growing investor confidence following the announcement of a strategic partnership aimed at revolutionizing quantum computing applications. Further boosting its prospects, analysts from Needham and B. Riley raised their price targets for D-Wave to $8.50 and $11, respectively. <3> A report from QuEra Computing, titled "Quantum Readiness Report 2025," indicates that the primary obstacles to adopting quantum computing in 2025 are high implementation costs, a shortage of skilled professionals, and unclear business value. The findings are based on a survey of over 750 (nearly 800) global participants, including academics, scientists, and industry professionals. The report specifies that 51% of respondents identified high costs as a top barrier, while 45% pointed to a lack of skilled talent and another 45% cited unclear business value. Despite these challenges, the report, published on January 22, 2025, also reveals growing confidence in the field, with a projected 20% increase in global quantum budgets for the year. <4> The U.S. Department of Energy's Office of Science announced a $625 million funding opportunity for National Quantum Information Science Research Centers.; The aim was to advance research in areas like quantum computing, communication, and sensing. <5> On January 16, 2025, the U.S. Department of Energy (DOE) announced $71 million in funding for 25 distinct projects in high-energy physics. [1] These projects will leverage emerging technologies in quantum information science to explore fundamental questions about the universe. [1] Selected through a competitive peer review process under the QuantISED 2.0 program, the initiatives will focus on developing quantum sensors to detect previously unobservable signals, such as those from dark matter, and advancing theories related to gravity and spacetime. [1, 2, 3] The funding will be distributed over a period of up to five years, with $20 million allocated for Fiscal Year 2025. [1, 2] <6> During a question-and-answer session with analysts at CES on January 7, 2025, Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang stated that "very useful" quantum computing was likely 15 to 30 years away. [1, 4, 11] He offered 20 years as a realistic timeframe for the technology to mature for widespread practical applications. [3, 4, 7] This assessment was widely seen as a conservative estimate from a key industry leader and had an immediate impact on the market. This program, supported by the NSF Quantum Leap Challenge Institute for Hybrid Quantum Architectures and Networks, aims to help educators bring cutting-edge quantum concepts into their classrooms. The broader initiative for the International Year of Quantum will commence with an opening ceremony at UNESCO Headquarters on February 4-5, 2025. <8> Quantum Computing Inc. (QCi) announced on December 17, 2024, that it has been awarded a prime contract by NASA's Goddard Space Flight Center. [1, 7] Under the contract, QCi will utilize its Dirac-3 entropy quantum optimization machine to address the complex 'phase unwrapping' problem for NASA. [1, 9] This process is crucial for optimally reconstructing images and extracting information from interferometric data generated by radar. [4] The project aims to demonstrate the superior capabilities of QCi's quantum optimization technology in solving NP-hard problems by improving solution quality and computational speed compared to classical computers. [1, 4] Success in this project is expected to bring long-term benefits to NASA by enhancing its big-data processing capabilities and could open doors for similar quantum applications in other fields. [2, 7, 9] This partnership is aimed at streamlining hybrid quantum-classical computing by allowing researchers and developers to design, simulate, and execute complex algorithms more efficiently. [8] The integration provides developers using the CUDA-Q environment with direct, pay-as-you-go access to a variety of quantum processing units (QPUs) on the Braket platform, including hardware from IonQ, Rigetti, IQM, and QuEra, while also offering Braket users a ready-to-use CUDA-Q environment for developing accelerated hybrid applications. [7, 8]
